source.text: וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן־אָדָ֔ם הִנָּבֵ֖א אֶל־הָרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְאָ֣מַרְתָּ֔ הָרֵי֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל שִׁמְע֖וּ דְּבַר־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And you, son of man, prophesy to [the] mountains of Israel and say: Mountains of Israel, hear [the] word of Yahweh.

en.L: Now you, son of man, prophesy to the mountains of Israel, and you will say, Mountains of Israel, hear the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Now, son of man, prophesy to the mountains of Israel. Say, Mountains of Israel, hear the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Son of man, prophesy to the mountains of Israel. Say to them, Mountains of Israel, listen to what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says.

decisions.choice: mountains of Israel: the reverse of chapter 6
decisions.reason: In 6:1-7 Ezekiel prophesied against the mountains of Israel, where the idols were worshiped. Now he prophesies to them with a promise. The message answers chapter 35: Edom, the mountain of Seir, will be desolate, and the mountains of Israel will be inhabited again.

decisions.choice: and you: the message continues from chapter 35
decisions.reason: The chapter begins with "And you", without the usual heading. It goes on from the message against Seir.

decisions.choice: listen to what the LORD says (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "listen to what the LORD says" for "hear the word of the LORD", as at 34:7. The message takes no quotation marks, by the rule set for Ezekiel.

source.text: כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה יַ֣עַן אָמַ֧ר הָאוֹיֵ֛ב עֲלֵיכֶ֖ם הֶאָ֑ח וּבָמ֣וֹת עוֹלָ֔ם לְמֽוֹרָשָׁ֖ה הָ֥יְתָה לָּֽנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Because the enemy has said against you, Aha! and, The ancient heights have become ours as a possession,

en.L: Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Because the enemy said about you, "Aha!" and, "The ancient heights have become our possession,"
en.B: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: The enemy said about you, "Aha! The ancient heights have become our property!"
en.R: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: Your enemy said about you, "Ha! Those old hills belong to us now!"

decisions.choice: the ancient heights: the age-old hills of the land
decisions.reason: The word *bamot* often means the hill shrines, the "high places". Here, with "ancient", it seems to mean the heights of the land itself, its hills that have stood from of old (Deuteronomy 32:13; 33:15).

decisions.choice: Aha!: a cry of gloating
decisions.reason: The same cry is used by the nations who rejoiced at Jerusalem's fall (25:3; 26:2).

decisions.choice: the enemy: Edom and the nations around
decisions.reason: Verse 5 names "the rest of the nations and all Edom" (35:10, 12).

decisions.choice: ancient heights (L, B); old hills (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording "high places" is not used here, because the word means the hills themselves (m1). The enemy's words take double quotation marks. Literal and Balanced end differently: Literal keeps the long sentence that runs on into verse 3; Balanced and Readable close the enemy's words with a full stop.

source.text: לָכֵן֙ הִנָּבֵ֣א וְאָמַרְתָּ֔ כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה יַ֣עַן בְּיַ֡עַן שַׁמּוֹת֩ וְשָׁאֹ֨ף אֶתְכֶ֜ם מִסָּבִ֗יב לִֽהְיוֹתְכֶ֤ם מֽוֹרָשָׁה֙ לִשְׁאֵרִ֣ית הַגּוֹיִ֔ם וַתֵּֽעֲל֛וּ עַל־שְׂפַ֥ת לָשׁ֖וֹן וְדִבַּת־עָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: therefore prophesy and say: Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Because, yes because, they made [you] desolate and crushed you from all around, so that you became a possession for the rest of the nations, and you were taken up on [the] lip of [the] tongue and [the] talk of people,

en.L: therefore prophesy and say, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Because, yes, because they made [you] desolate and crushed you from every side, so that you became a possession of the remaining nations, and you became the talk of gossips and the whispering of people,
en.B: Therefore prophesy and say, The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: They made you desolate and hounded you from every side, so that you became the property of the rest of the nations, and people talked and gossiped about you.
en.R: So prophesy and say, This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: Enemies attacked you from every side and left you empty. Other nations took you for themselves, and people talked about you and made fun of you.

decisions.choice: because, yes because: the Hebrew doubles the word
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "because, because" for emphasis. The repeated "therefore" and "because" in verses 2-7 pile up the reasons before the promise of verse 8.

decisions.choice: taken up on the lip of the tongue: made the subject of gossip
decisions.reason: To be "on the lips" of people is to be talked about and mocked (compare Deuteronomy 28:37).

decisions.choice: crushed you: the verb is uncertain
decisions.reason: The verb may mean "trample" or "pant after", that is, hunt eagerly. Either way the land was set upon from every side.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD (L); The Lord GOD says this (B); This is what the Lord GOD says (R)
decisions.reason: The formula as set at 2:4. Literal brackets the object "you" that English needs.

source.text: לָכֵן֙ הָרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל שִׁמְע֖וּ דְּבַר־אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה כֹּֽה־אָמַ֣ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְ֠הוִה לֶהָרִ֨ים וְלַגְּבָע֜וֹת לָאֲפִיקִ֣ים וְלַגֵּאָי֗וֹת וְלֶחֳרָב֤וֹת הַשֹּֽׁמְמוֹת֙ וְלֶעָרִ֣ים הַנֶּעֱזָב֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָי֤וּ לְבַז֙ וּלְלַ֔עַג לִשְׁאֵרִ֥ית הַגּוֹיִ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר מִסָּבִֽיב׃ס

records.literal_gloss: therefore, mountains of Israel, hear [the] word of [the] Lord Yahweh: Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh to the mountains and to the hills, to the ravines and to the valleys, to the desolate wastes and to the forsaken cities, which have become plunder and mockery to the rest of the nations that [are] all around,

en.L: therefore, mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} to the mountains and the hills, to the ravines and the valleys, to the desolate ruins and the deserted cities that have become plunder and a mockery to the rest of the nations all around,
en.B: therefore, mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}. The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this to the mountains and hills, the ravines and valleys, the desolate ruins and the abandoned towns that have been plundered and mocked by the rest of the nations around them.
en.R: Listen, mountains of Israel, to what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says. This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says to the mountains, the hills, the ravines and the valleys, to the empty ruins and the towns where no one lives. The nations around you have robbed you and laughed at you.

decisions.choice: mountains, hills, ravines and valleys: as in 6:3
decisions.reason: The same four words were used in 6:3 for the judgment of the land. Now the same places hear a word of hope.

decisions.choice: therefore: the sentence runs on into verse 5
decisions.reason: The address in verse 4 runs on into the formula of verse 5, which repeats "therefore, thus says the Lord GOD" before the message itself.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD (L); The Lord GOD says this (B); This is what the Lord GOD says (R)
decisions.reason: The formula as set at 2:4. The words "to the mountains ..." follow the formula, as in 6:3. Literal and Balanced end with a comma, since the sentence runs on into verse 5.

source.text: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה־אָמַר֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ אִם־לֹ֠א בְּאֵ֨שׁ קִנְאָתִ֥י דִבַּ֛רְתִּי עַל־שְׁאֵרִ֥ית הַגּוֹיִ֖ם וְעַל־אֱד֣וֹם כֻּלָּ֑א אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָתְנֽוּ־אֶת־אַרְצִ֣י׀לָ֠הֶם לְמ֨וֹרָשָׁ֜ה בְּשִׂמְחַ֤ת כָּל־לֵבָב֙ בִּשְׁאָ֣ט נֶ֔פֶשׁ לְמַ֥עַן מִגְרָשָׁ֖הּ לָבַֽז׃

records.literal_gloss: therefore thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Surely in [the] fire of my jealousy I have spoken against the rest of the nations and against Edom, all of it, who gave my land to themselves as a possession with joy of all heart, with contempt of soul, so that its pasture [would be] plunder.

en.L: therefore thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Surely I have spoken in the fire of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} jealousy against the remnant of the nations and against Edom, all of it, who gave {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} land to themselves as a possession with wholehearted joy [and] with contempt in [their] soul, so that its pastureland [would become] plunder.
en.B: therefore the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: In the fire of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} jealousy I have spoken out against the other nations and against all of Edom. With hearts full of glee and with utter contempt, they took {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} land for themselves, so that they could plunder its pastures.
en.R: So this is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: I am burning with jealous anger, and I have spoken out against the other nations and against all of Edom. They were very glad to take {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} land for themselves. They hated {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, and they wanted to rob them of their pastures.

decisions.choice: the fire of my jealousy: the LORD's zeal for his land and people
decisions.reason: The LORD's jealousy is his burning zeal for what belongs to him (Deuteronomy 4:24; Zechariah 1:14; 8:2). The land is "my land": Edom has seized what is the LORD's.

decisions.choice: with contempt of soul: with utter scorn
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used of the Philistines' scorn in 25:15 and of Edom's in 25:6.

decisions.choice: so that its pasture would be plunder: the sense is uncertain
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is hard. It may mean "in order to plunder its pastureland" or "to drive it out as plunder". The point is that the nations wanted the land for their own gain.

decisions.choice: I am burning with jealous anger; They hated my people (R)
decisions.reason: Readable gives the picture of fire in plain words and says what "contempt of soul" means.

source.text: לָכֵ֕ן הִנָּבֵ֖א עַל־אַדְמַ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְאָמַרְתָּ֡ לֶהָרִ֣ים וְ֠לַגְּבָעוֹת לָאֲפִיקִ֨ים וְלַגֵּאָי֜וֹת כֹּֽה־אָמַ֣ר׀אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה הִנְנִ֨י בְקִנְאָתִ֤י וּבַחֲמָתִי֙ דִּבַּ֔רְתִּי יַ֛עַן כְּלִמַּ֥ת גּוֹיִ֖ם נְשָׂאתֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore prophesy concerning [the] land of Israel and say to [the] mountains and to [the] hills, to the ravines and to the valleys: Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Here I, in my jealousy and in my wrath, I have spoken, because [the] insult of nations you have borne.

en.L: Therefore prophesy concerning the land of Israel, and say to the mountains and the hills, to the ravines and the valleys, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Look, I, in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} jealousy and in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath, have spoken, because the insults of the nations you have borne.
en.B: Therefore prophesy about the land of Israel and say to the mountains and hills, to the ravines and valleys, The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: I have spoken in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} jealousy and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath, because you have suffered the scorn of the nations.
en.R: So prophesy about the land of Israel. Speak to the mountains, the hills, the ravines and the valleys. Tell them, This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: I am speaking in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} jealousy and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger, because the nations have insulted you.

decisions.choice: my jealousy and my wrath because you have borne the insult of the nations
decisions.reason: The anger once turned against Israel (5:13) is now turned against the nations that mocked it. The land has borne enough shame (verse 15; 34:29).

decisions.choice: wrath (L, B); anger (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *chemah* in Ezekiel.

source.text: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה אֲנִ֖י נָשָׂ֣אתִי אֶת־יָדִ֑י אִם־לֹ֤א הַגּוֹיִם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לָכֶ֣ם מִסָּבִ֔יב הֵ֖מָּה כְּלִמָּתָ֥םיִשָּֽׂאוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: I have lifted my hand: surely the nations that [are] around you, they will bear their insult.

en.L: Therefore thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: I have lifted {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand: surely the nations that are around you will themselves bear their insults.
en.B: Therefore the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: I have raised {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand in an oath that the nations around you will themselves suffer scorn.
en.R: So this is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: I make a solemn promise: the nations around you will be insulted in their turn.

decisions.choice: I have lifted my hand: I swear
decisions.reason: To lift the hand is to take an oath (20:5-6; Exodus 6:8). The LORD swears that the nations will suffer the shame they put on Israel.

decisions.choice: I have lifted my hand (L); I have raised my hand in an oath (B); I make a solemn promise (R)
decisions.reason: The wording used for this oath in 20:5 at Literal and Balanced. Readable says what it means.

source.text: וְאַתֶּ֞ם הָרֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ עַנְפְּכֶ֣ם תִּתֵּ֔נוּ וּפֶרְיְכֶ֥ם תִּשְׂא֖וּ לְעַמִּ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּ֥י קֵרְב֖וּ לָבֽוֹא׃

records.literal_gloss: But you, mountains of Israel, your branches you will put forth, and your fruit you will bear for my people Israel, for they are near to come.

en.L: But you, mountains of Israel, will put forth your branches and bear your fruit for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel, for they will soon come.
en.B: But you, mountains of Israel, will put out your branches and produce your fruit for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel, because they will soon come home.
en.R: But you, mountains of Israel, will grow branches again and produce fruit for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel. They will soon come home.

decisions.choice: they are near to come: the return from exile is close
decisions.reason: The exiles' return is near. The land itself is told to get ready for them by bearing fruit again.

decisions.choice: your branches and your fruit: the reverse of the curse
decisions.reason: The land that lay barren under the covenant curses (Leviticus 26:20) will be fruitful again (34:27).

source.text: כִּ֖י הִנְנִ֣י אֲלֵיכֶ֑ם וּפָנִ֣יתִי אֲלֵיכֶ֔ם וְנֶעֱבַדְתֶּ֖ם וְנִזְרַעְתֶּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: For here I [am] for you, and I will turn to you, and you will be tilled and sown.

en.L: For look, I [am] for you, and I will turn to you, and you will be tilled and sown.
en.B: For I am on your side, and I will turn to you with favor. You will be plowed and planted.
en.R: I am on your side. I will take care of you. People will plow your fields and plant seeds in them.

decisions.choice: here I am for you: the reverse of "I am against you"
decisions.reason: Ezekiel often says "Here I am against you" (5:8; 13:8; 35:3). Now the LORD says "I am for you", using the same words with a different preposition.

decisions.choice: I will turn to you: I will look on you with favor
decisions.reason: Leviticus 26:9 uses the same words: "I will turn to you and make you fruitful".

decisions.choice: on your side (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "I am for you" means. Literal keeps "look", the word the book uses for the Hebrew *hinneh*.

source.text: וְהִרְבֵּיתִ֤י עֲלֵיכֶם֙ אָדָ֔ם כָּל־בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל כֻּלֹּ֑ה וְנֹֽשְׁבוּ֙ הֶֽעָרִ֔ים וְהֶחֳרָב֖וֹת תִּבָּנֶֽינָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will multiply on you people, all [the] house of Israel, all of it; and the cities will be inhabited, and the ruins will be rebuilt.

en.L: And I will multiply people on you, the whole house of Israel, all of it; and the cities will be inhabited, and the ruins will be rebuilt.
en.B: I will multiply the people living on you, the whole house of Israel, every one of them. The towns will be lived in, and the ruins rebuilt.
en.R: I will make the number of people on your land grow, all the people of Israel. People will live in the towns again, and the ruins will be built again.

decisions.choice: all the house of Israel, all of it: the whole people, north and south
decisions.reason: The promise is for all Israel, not only Judah. Chapter 37 shows the two kingdoms joined again (37:15-22).

decisions.choice: people (L)
decisions.reason: The word *'adam* here means human beings in general, set beside animals in verse 11; it is "people" at every level, which needs no gender setting.

source.text: וְהִרְבֵּיתִ֧י עֲלֵיכֶ֛ם אָדָ֥ם וּבְהֵמָ֖ה וְרָב֣וּ וּפָר֑וּ וְהוֹשַׁבְתִּ֨י אֶתְכֶ֜ם כְּקַדְמֽוֹתֵיכֶ֗ם וְהֵטִֽבֹתִי֙ מֵרִאשֹׁ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם וִֽידַעְתֶּ֖ם כִּֽי־אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will multiply on you people and animals, and they will increase and be fruitful; and I will make you inhabited as in your former times, and I will do more good than at your beginnings; and you will know that I [am] Yahweh.

en.L: And I will multiply people and animals on you, and they will increase and be fruitful; and I will settle you as in your former times, and do more good [to you] than at your beginnings; and you will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: I will multiply people and animals on you, and they will increase and be fruitful. I will settle people on you as in the past, and I will make you more prosperous than you were at first. Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: I will make the number of people and animals on your land grow. They will have many children and young ones. I will let people live on you as they did long ago, and I will make things better for you than they were at the beginning. Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: they will increase and be fruitful: Genesis 1:28
decisions.reason: The words recall the blessing of creation and of the patriarchs (Genesis 1:28; 9:1; 35:11) and Leviticus 26:9. The land will be blessed as at the beginning, and more.

decisions.choice: they will increase and be fruitful: missing in the Septuagint
decisions.reason: The Septuagint does not have these words. The standard Hebrew text is kept.

decisions.choice: the refrain as settled
decisions.reason: The settled wording of the refrain ("and you will know that I [am] the LORD" / "Then you will know that I am the LORD"; see 6:7).

source.text: וְהוֹלַכְתִּי֩ עֲלֵיכֶ֨ם אָדָ֜ם אֶת־עַמִּ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וִֽירֵשׁ֔וּךָ וְהָיִ֥יתָ לָהֶ֖ם לְנַחֲלָ֑ה וְלֹא־תוֹסִ֥ף ע֖וֹד לְשַׁכְּלָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And I will make walk on you people, my people Israel, and they will possess you, and you will be their inheritance, and you will no longer bereave them.

en.L: And I will make people walk on you, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel; and they will take possession of you, and you will become their inheritance; and never again will you bereave them [of children].
en.B: I will lead people to walk on you again, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel. They will take possession of you, and you will be their heritage. You will never again rob them of their children.
en.R: I will bring {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel to walk on your land again. They will own you, and you will belong to them. You will never again take their children away from them.

decisions.choice: you will no longer bereave them: the land will no longer take their children
decisions.reason: The land is pictured as a devourer that has made parents childless through famine, war and disaster (verses 13-14). The spies once said it was "a land that devours its inhabitants" (Numbers 13:32).

decisions.choice: [of children] (L); rob them of their children (B); take their children away (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to make childless. Each level says whose loss is meant.

source.text: כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה יַ֚עַן אֹמְרִ֣ים לָכֶ֔ם אֹכֶ֥לֶת אָדָ֖ם אָ֑תְּ וּמְשַׁכֶּ֥לֶת גּוֹיַ֖יִךְ הָיִֽית׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Because they are saying to you, You devour people, and you have been bereaving your nations,

en.L: Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Because they say to you, "You devour people, and you have bereaved your nation [of its children],"
en.B: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: People say about you, "You devour people, and you rob your nation of its children."
en.R: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: People say that your land eats up its people and takes away the children of your nation.

decisions.choice: your nations: the reading tradition
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew has the plural, "your nations"; the scribes' marginal reading has the singular, "your nation". The sense is the same: the people of the land.

decisions.choice: you devour people: Numbers 13:32
decisions.reason: The spies called the land "a land that devours its inhabitants" (Numbers 13:32). The nations now say the same, pointing to the disasters that fell on Israel.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD (L); The Lord GOD says this (B); This is what the Lord GOD says (R)
decisions.reason: The formula as set at 2:4. The people's words take double quotation marks at Literal and Balanced; Readable reports them. The sentence runs on into verse 14 at Literal.

source.text: לָכֵ֗ן אָדָם֙ לֹא־תֹ֣אכְלִי ע֔וֹד וְגוֹיַ֖יִךְ לֹ֣א תְשַׁכְּלִי־ע֑וֹד נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: therefore people you will no longer devour, and your nations you will no longer bereave, declares [the] Lord Yahweh.

en.L: therefore you will no longer devour people, and you will no longer bereave your nation, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Therefore you will no longer devour people or rob your nation of its children, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: But you will never again eat up people or take away the children of your nation, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: bereave: the reading tradition
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew has "cause to stumble", as in verse 15; the scribes' marginal reading has "bereave", as in verse 13. The two verbs differ by one letter. The marginal reading is followed here.

decisions.choice: declares the Lord GOD (L, B); says the Lord GOD (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *ne'um Adonai YHWH*.

source.text: וְלֹא־אַשְׁמִ֨יעַ אֵלַ֤יִךְ עוֹד֙ כְּלִמַּ֣ת הַגּוֹיִ֔ם וְחֶרְפַּ֥ת עַמִּ֖ים לֹ֣א תִשְׂאִי־ע֑וֹד וְגוֹיַ֨יִךְ֙ לֹא־תַכְשִׁ֣לִי ע֔וֹד נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And I will no longer make heard against you [the] insult of the nations, and [the] reproach of peoples you will no longer bear, and your nations you will no longer cause to stumble, declares [the] Lord Yahweh.

en.L: And I will no longer let you hear the insults of the nations, and you will no longer bear the reproach of the peoples, and you will no longer make your nation stumble, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: I will no longer let you hear the nations' insults, and you will no longer bear the scorn of the peoples or make your nation fall, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: I will not let the nations insult you anymore. You will not have to put up with their mocking anymore. And you will not make your nation fall again, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: cause to stumble: the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: Here both the written text and the marginal reading have "cause to stumble". Some manuscripts read "bereave", as in verse 14. The land will no longer be the place where the nation falls.

decisions.choice: the insult of the nations: the end of Israel's shame
decisions.reason: The nations mocked Israel for its ruin, and through it they mocked the LORD (verse 20). That shame will end.

source.text: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:

en.L: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:
en.B: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave me this message:

decisions.choice: the word of the LORD came to me: why the LORD will act
decisions.reason: A new message explains why the LORD will restore Israel: not because Israel deserves it, but for the sake of his holy name (verses 22, 32).

decisions.choice: The word of the LORD came to me, saying: (L); The word of the LORD came to me: (B); The LORD gave me this message: (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this formula in Jeremiah and Ezekiel. What follows is the LORD's message, which takes no quotation marks, by the rule set for Ezekiel.

source.text: בֶּן־אָדָ֗ם בֵּ֤ית יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ יֹשְׁבִ֣ים עַל־אַדְמָתָ֔ם וַיְטַמְּא֣וּ אוֹתָ֔הּ בְּדַרְכָּ֖ם וּבַעֲלִֽילוֹתָ֑ם כְּטֻמְאַת֙ הַנִּדָּ֔ה הָיְתָ֥ה דַרְכָּ֖ם לְפָנָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Son of man, [the] house of Israel [were] dwelling on their soil, and they defiled it by their ways and by their deeds; like the uncleanness of menstruation was their way before me.

en.L: Son of man, when the house of Israel lived on their own soil, they made it unclean by their ways and their deeds; their way was before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} like the uncleanness of a woman in her menstruation.
en.B: Son of man, while the house of Israel was living in its own land, they made it unclean by their conduct and deeds. To {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} their conduct was like the impurity of a woman during her period.
en.R: Son of man, when the people of Israel lived in their own land, they made it unclean by the way they lived and the things they did. To {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, the way they lived was as unclean as a woman during her monthly period.

decisions.choice: the uncleanness of menstruation: ritual impurity under the Law
decisions.reason: Under the Law a woman was ritually unclean during her monthly period, and anything she touched became unclean (Leviticus 15:19-24). This was not a matter of sin, but it kept a person from the sanctuary. The picture says that Israel's conduct made the land unfit for the LORD's presence.

decisions.choice: they defiled the land: Leviticus 18:24-28
decisions.reason: The Law warned that if Israel did what the nations did, the land would be defiled and would vomit them out (Leviticus 18:24-28; Numbers 35:33-34).

decisions.choice: during her period (B); during her monthly period (R)
decisions.reason: Literal follows the Hebrew; Balanced and Readable state the meaning plainly, as in 18:6.

source.text: וָאֶשְׁפֹּ֤ךְ חֲמָתִי֙ עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם עַל־הַדָּ֖ם אֲשֶׁר־שָׁפְכ֣וּ עַל־הָאָ֑רֶץ וּבְגִלּוּלֵיהֶ֖ם טִמְּאֽוּהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And I poured out my wrath on them for the blood that they had poured out on the land, and with their idols they had defiled it.

en.L: So I poured out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath on them for the blood that they had poured out on the land; and with their filthy idols they had defiled it.
en.B: So I poured out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath on them because of the blood they had shed in the land and because they had defiled it with their idols.
en.R: So I poured out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger on them, because they had murdered people in the land and had made it unclean by worshiping idols.

decisions.choice: I poured out ... they had poured out: a play on the verb
decisions.reason: The same verb is used for the blood they shed and the anger the LORD poured on them. Their punishment matches their crime.

decisions.choice: blood and idols: violence and false worship
decisions.reason: The two sins that defile the land throughout Ezekiel: bloodshed (22:2-4) and idolatry (chapters 6; 8). The verse is missing in the Septuagint's part after "on them".

decisions.choice: wrath (L, B), anger (R); filthy idols (L), idols (B, R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *chemah* and *gillulim*.

source.text: וָאָפִ֤יץ אֹתָם֙ בַּגּוֹיִ֔ם וַיִּזָּר֖וּ בָּאֲרָצ֑וֹת כְּדַרְכָּ֥ם וְכַעֲלִילוֹתָ֖ם שְׁפַטְתִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And I scattered them among the nations, and they were dispersed through the lands; according to their ways and according to their deeds I judged them.

en.L: And I scattered them among the nations, and they were dispersed in the lands; according to their ways and their deeds I judged them.
en.B: I scattered them among the nations and dispersed them through the lands. I judged them by their conduct and their deeds.
en.R: I scattered them among the nations and sent them away to many countries. I punished them for the way they lived and the things they did.

decisions.choice: according to their ways I judged them: the exile was just
decisions.reason: The scattering was the LORD's judgment, the curse the covenant warned of (Leviticus 26:33; Deuteronomy 28:64).

source.text: וַיָּב֗וֹא אֶל־הַגּוֹיִם֙ אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֣אוּ שָׁ֔ם וַֽיְחַלְּל֖וּ אֶת־שֵׁ֣ם קָדְשִׁ֑י בֶּאֱמֹ֤ר לָהֶם֙ עַם־יְהוָ֣ה אֵ֔לֶּה וּמֵאַרְצ֖וֹ יָצָֽאוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they came to the nations where they came, and they profaned my holy name, in that it was said of them, These [are the] people of Yahweh, and from his land they have gone out.

en.L: And they came to the nations where they went, and they profaned {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy name, in that people said of them, "These [are] the people of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and yet they have had to leave {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} land."
en.B: Among the nations they came to, they profaned {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy name, for people said of them, "These are the people of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and yet they had to leave {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} land."
en.R: But wherever they went, they made people disrespect {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy name. People said about them, "These are {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s people, but they had to leave {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} land."

decisions.choice: they profaned my holy name: the exile made the LORD look powerless
decisions.reason: The nations judged a god by the fortunes of his people. Seeing Israel driven from its land, they concluded that the LORD could not protect his own. So Israel's presence among the nations, as exiles, brought dishonor on the LORD's name.

decisions.choice: my holy name: the LORD himself, as he is known
decisions.reason: The name stands for the person and his reputation. It is "holy" because it belongs to the holy God (20:39; 39:7).

decisions.choice: made people disrespect my holy name (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what "profaned" means here: it was the nations who spoke of the LORD with contempt because of the exiles (m1). The words of the nations take double quotation marks; the pronoun "his" for the LORD in them takes the deity_pronoun setting.

source.text: וָאֶחְמֹ֖ל עַל־שֵׁ֣ם קָדְשִׁ֑י אֲשֶׁ֤ר חִלְּל֨וּהוּ֙ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בַּגּוֹיִ֖ם אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֥אוּ שָֽׁמָּה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And I had pity on my holy name, which they had profaned, the house of Israel, among the nations where they went.

en.L: But I had concern for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy name, which they had profaned, the house of Israel, among the nations to which they had gone.
en.B: But I was concerned for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy name, the name the house of Israel profaned in the nations they went to.
en.R: But I cared about the honor of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy name, which the people of Israel had disgraced among the nations where they went.

decisions.choice: I had pity on: I was concerned for
decisions.reason: The verb means to feel pity or to spare. Here the LORD cares for the honor of his name.

decisions.choice: had concern for (L); was concerned for (B)
decisions.reason: English does not "pity" a name; each level gives the sense (m1).

source.text: לָכֵ֞ן אֱמֹ֣ר לְבֵֽית־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה לֹ֧א לְמַעַנְכֶ֛ם אֲנִ֥י עֹשֶׂ֖ה בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּ֤י אִם־לְשֵׁם־קָדְשִׁי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חִלַּלְתֶּ֔ם בַּגּוֹיִ֖ם אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֥אתֶם שָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore say to [the] house of Israel: Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Not for your sake [am] I acting, house of Israel, but for my holy name, which you have profaned among the nations where you went.

en.L: Therefore say to the house of Israel, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: It is not for your sake that I am about to act, house of Israel, but for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy name, which you profaned in the nations that you came to.
en.B: Therefore say to the house of Israel, The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: I am not about to act for your sake, house of Israel, but for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy name, which you have profaned in the nations you went to.
en.R: So tell the people of Israel, This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: People of Israel, I am going to act, but not because of you. I will do it for the honor of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy name, which you have disgraced among the nations where you went.

decisions.choice: not for your sake but for my holy name: grace that is not earned
decisions.reason: The LORD will restore Israel, not because they have earned it, but to show who he is. The same reason is given in 20:9, 14, 22, 44. It leaves no room for pride (verse 32), and it makes the promise sure, since it rests on the LORD and not on Israel.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD (L); The Lord GOD says this (B); This is what the Lord GOD says (R)
decisions.reason: The formula as set at 2:4.

source.text: וְקִדַּשְׁתִּ֞י אֶת־שְׁמִ֣י הַגָּד֗וֹל הַֽמְחֻלָּל֙ בַּגּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר חִלַּלְתֶּ֖ם בְּתוֹכָ֑ם וְיָדְע֨וּ הַגּוֹיִ֜ם כִּי־אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֗ה נְאֻם֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה בְּהִקָּדְשִׁ֥י בָכֶ֖ם לְעֵינֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will show holy my great name, which has been profaned among the nations, which you have profaned in their midst; and the nations will know that I [am] Yahweh, declares [the] Lord Yahweh, when I show myself holy through you before their eyes.

en.L: And I will show {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} great name to be holy, [the name] profaned among the nations, which you profaned among them; and the nations will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, when through you I show {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} holy before their eyes.
en.B: I will show that {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} great name is holy, the name that has been dishonored among the nations, which you dishonored among them. Then the nations will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, as I display {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holiness through you before their eyes.
en.R: I will show the nations how holy {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} great name is. You disgraced it among them, but I will show them that I am holy by what I do for you. Then the nations will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: I will show holy my name ... show myself holy: make known that I am holy
decisions.reason: The verb means to treat or show as holy. The LORD will make his holiness plain to the nations by what he does for his people, as he did when he brought them out of Egypt (20:41; 28:22, 25; 38:16, 23).

decisions.choice: verses 23b-38: missing in one early Greek manuscript
decisions.reason: An early Greek papyrus of Ezekiel (Papyrus 967) does not have the text from the middle of this verse to the end of the chapter, and it places chapter 37 after chapters 38-39. Other Greek manuscripts and all Hebrew ones have the passage. The standard Hebrew text is kept.

decisions.choice: the refrain with "the nations"
decisions.reason: The settled wording of the refrain, with "the nations" as the subject. Readable puts "says the Lord GOD" at the end so that its short sentences keep the order of thought.

source.text: וְלָקַחְתִּ֤י אֶתְכֶם֙ מִן־הַגּוֹיִ֔ם וְקִבַּצְתִּ֥י אֶתְכֶ֖ם מִכָּל־הָאֲרָצ֑וֹת וְהֵבֵאתִ֥י אֶתְכֶ֖ם אֶל־אַדְמַתְכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will take you from the nations and gather you from all the lands, and I will bring you into your land.

en.L: For I will take you from the nations and gather you from all the lands, and bring you into your own land.
en.B: I will take you out of the nations, gather you from every land and bring you back to your own country.
en.R: I will take you out of the nations. I will gather you from all the other countries and bring you back to your own land.

decisions.choice: I will take you, gather you, bring you: the return from exile
decisions.reason: The first of the things the LORD will do "for his name": bring his people home (11:17; 20:41-42; 34:13). The return will show the nations that he is able to keep his people.

source.text: וְזָרַקְתִּ֧י עֲלֵיכֶ֛ם מַ֥יִם טְהוֹרִ֖ים וּטְהַרְתֶּ֑ם מִכֹּ֧ל טֻמְאוֹתֵיכֶ֛ם וּמִכָּל־גִּלּ֥וּלֵיכֶ֖ם אֲטַהֵ֥ר אֶתְכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will sprinkle on you clean water, and you will be clean from all your uncleannesses, and from all your idols I will cleanse you.

en.L: And I will sprinkle on you clean water, and you will be clean from all your uncleannesses, and from all your filthy idols I will cleanse you.
en.B: I will sprinkle pure water over you, and you will be clean. From all your impurities and from all your idols I will make you clean.
en.R: I will sprinkle you with pure water, and you will be clean. I will wash away everything that made you unclean, and I will take away all your idols.

decisions.choice: I will sprinkle clean water on you: the water of cleansing in the Law
decisions.reason: The Law used sprinkled water to cleanse people from ritual impurity, for example the water of purification used for one who had touched a dead body (Numbers 19:13-20). Here the LORD himself cleanses his people from the impurity of verses 17-18. Psalm 51:9 and Hebrews 10:22 use the same picture.

decisions.choice: clean water ... a new spirit: John 3:5
decisions.reason: When Jesus tells Nicodemus that no one can enter the kingdom of God unless they are born "of water and the Spirit" (John 3:5), he seems to take up this promise of cleansing water and a new spirit (verses 25-27), which a teacher of Israel should have known (John 3:10).

decisions.choice: filthy idols (L); idols (B, R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *gillulim*.

source.text: וְנָתַתִּ֤י לָכֶם֙ לֵ֣ב חָדָ֔שׁ וְר֥וּחַ חֲדָשָׁ֖ה אֶתֵּ֣ן בְּקִרְבְּכֶ֑ם וַהֲסִ֨רֹתִ֜י אֶת־לֵ֤ב הָאֶ֨בֶן֙ מִבְּשַׂרְכֶ֔ם וְנָתַתִּ֥י לָכֶ֖ם לֵ֥ב בָּשָֽׂר׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will give you a new heart, and a new spirit I will put within you, and I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh.

en.L: And I will give you a new heart, and a new spirit I will put within you; and I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh.
en.B: I will give you a new heart, and I will place a new spirit within you. I will take the heart of stone out of your bodies and give you a heart of flesh.
en.R: I will give you a new heart and place a new spirit in you. I will take away your heart of stone, which is hard, and give you a heart of flesh, which is tender and alive.

decisions.choice: a new heart and a new spirit; the heart of stone and the heart of flesh: 11:19
decisions.reason: The LORD gave this promise in almost the same words in 11:19, and in 18:31 he told Israel to make for itself "a new heart and a new spirit". What he commanded there he promises to give here. Jeremiah promises the same inner change in the new covenant (Jeremiah 31:33; 32:39), and Paul uses the picture of hearts of flesh in 2 Corinthians 3:3.

decisions.choice: heart and spirit; stone and flesh
decisions.reason: As in 11:19, the heart is the seat of thought and will as well as feeling, and the spirit is the inner life. A heart of stone cannot respond to God; a heart of flesh is alive and able to respond. "Spirit" here is the people's own spirit, written with a small letter; in verse 27 the LORD speaks of "my Spirit".

decisions.choice: heart of stone, heart of flesh (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced reuse the published wording of 11:19, with "you" for "them" and "a new heart" for "one heart". Readable keeps the words "heart of stone" and "heart of flesh" here, where 11:19 explains the pictures instead, because this is the best-known form of the promise; it adds a short explanation of each.

source.text: וְאֶת־רוּחִ֖י אֶתֵּ֣ן בְּקִרְבְּכֶ֑ם וְעָשִׂ֗יתִי אֵ֤ת אֲשֶׁר־בְּחֻקַּי֙ תֵּלֵ֔כוּ וּמִשְׁפָּטַ֥י תִּשְׁמְר֖וּ וַעֲשִׂיתֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And my Spirit I will put within you, and I will cause that in my statutes you walk, and my judgments you keep and do.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Spirit I will put within you, and I will cause you to walk in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes and to keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} judgments and do [them].
en.B: I will put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Spirit within you and make you follow {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes and carefully keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rulings.
en.R: I will put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Spirit in you. I will make you want to live by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} laws and to obey {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rules carefully.

decisions.choice: my Spirit: the LORD's own Spirit
decisions.reason: In verse 26 the new spirit is the people's; here the LORD gives his own Spirit, who will move them to obey. The same promise comes in 37:14 and 39:29, and Joel 3:1-2 promises that the LORD will pour out his Spirit on all people. The New Testament speaks of the gift of the Spirit in these terms (John 3:5; 2 Corinthians 3:3-6).

decisions.choice: I will cause you to walk in my statutes: obedience as the LORD's gift
decisions.reason: The LORD does not only command; he gives the will and the power to obey. This answers Israel's long failure to keep his statutes (20:13, 21).

decisions.choice: Spirit, capitalized; statutes, judgments (L); statutes, rulings (B); laws, rules (R)
decisions.reason: Isaiah's rule, followed at 2:2, capitalizes "Spirit" for God's Spirit. The two words for the LORD's commands follow the settled wording in Ezekiel. Literal brackets "them".

source.text: וִישַׁבְתֶּ֣ם בָּאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֖תִּי לַאֲבֹֽתֵיכֶ֑ם וִהְיִ֤יתֶם לִי֙ לְעָ֔ם וְאָ֣נֹכִ֔י אֶהְיֶ֥ה לָכֶ֖ם לֵאלֹהִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will dwell in the land that I gave to your fathers, and you will be my people, and I will be your God.

en.L: And you will live in the land that I gave your fathers, and you will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, and I will be your God.
en.B: You will live in the land I gave to your ancestors. You will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, and I will be your God.
en.R: You will live in the land I gave your ancestors. You will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, and I will be your God.

decisions.choice: you will be my people, and I will be your God: the covenant formula
decisions.reason: The central promise of the covenant (11:20; 14:11; 37:23, 27; Jeremiah 31:33).

decisions.choice: ancestors (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "fathers"; Balanced and Readable say "ancestors", which is what the word means here.

source.text: וְהוֹשַׁעְתִּ֣י אֶתְכֶ֔ם מִכֹּ֖ל טֻמְאֽוֹתֵיכֶ֑ם וְקָרָ֤אתִי אֶל־הַדָּגָן֙ וְהִרְבֵּיתִ֣י אֹת֔וֹ וְלֹא־אֶתֵּ֥ן עֲלֵיכֶ֖ם רָעָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will save you from all your uncleannesses; and I will call for the grain and make it plentiful, and I will not lay famine on you.

en.L: And I will save you out of all your uncleannesses; and I will summon the grain and multiply it, and I will not bring famine on you.
en.B: I will save you from all your impurities. I will call for the grain and make it abundant, and I will not send famine on you.
en.R: I will save you from everything that makes you unclean. I will order the grain to grow, and there will be plenty of it. I will not let you go hungry.

decisions.choice: I will call for the grain: as a master summons a servant
decisions.reason: The LORD commands the harvest, as he summoned famine against the land in 2 Kings 8:1 and Psalm 105:16.

decisions.choice: I will save you from all your uncleannesses
decisions.reason: The cleansing of verse 25 is the LORD's saving work, not the people's own.

source.text: וְהִרְבֵּיתִי֙ אֶת־פְּרִ֣י הָעֵ֔ץ וּתְנוּבַ֖ת הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה לְמַ֗עַן אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹ֣א תִקְח֥וּ ע֛וֹד חֶרְפַּ֥ת רָעָ֖ב בַּגּוֹיִֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will multiply the fruit of the tree and the produce of the field, so that you will no longer receive [the] reproach of famine among the nations.

en.L: And I will multiply the fruit of the tree and the produce of the field, so that you will no longer suffer the disgrace of famine among the nations.
en.B: I will make the fruit trees and the fields produce plenty, so that you will never again suffer the disgrace of famine among the nations.
en.R: I will make the trees produce lots of fruit and the fields grow plenty of crops. The nations will never again laugh at you because you have no food.

decisions.choice: the reproach of famine among the nations: the shame of hunger
decisions.reason: Famine was a sign of a god's curse, and the nations mocked Israel for it (34:29). Plenty will end the shame.

source.text: וּזְכַרְתֶּם֙ אֶת־דַּרְכֵיכֶ֣ם הָרָעִ֔ים וּמַעַלְלֵיכֶ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא־טוֹבִ֑ים וּנְקֹֽטֹתֶם֙ בִּפְנֵיכֶ֔ם עַ֚ל עֲוֺנֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם וְעַ֖ל תּוֹעֲבֽוֹתֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will remember your evil ways and your deeds that [were] not good, and you will loathe yourselves for your iniquities and for your abominations.

en.L: And you will remember your ways, the evil [ones], and your doings that [were] not good, and you will feel loathing in your own sight for your iniquities and for your abominations.
en.B: Then you will call to mind your evil ways and the things you did that were not good, and you will be disgusted with yourselves for your guilt and your detestable practices.
en.R: Then you will remember the evil way you lived and the wrong things you did, and you will hate yourselves for your sins and your disgusting practices.

decisions.choice: you will loathe yourselves: you will be disgusted with yourselves
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "you will loathe in your faces", that is, in your own sight. As in 6:9 and 20:43, the LORD's kindness, not his punishment, brings them to see their sin for what it was.

decisions.choice: you will remember: repentance after grace
decisions.reason: In Ezekiel shame and repentance follow the LORD's gift (16:61-63; 20:43). The order shows that the restoration is pure grace.

decisions.choice: iniquities, abominations (L); guilt, detestable practices (B); sins, disgusting practices (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *'awon* and *to'evah*.

source.text: לֹ֧א לְמַעַנְכֶ֣ם אֲנִֽי־עֹשֶׂ֗ה נְאֻם֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה יִוָּדַ֖ע לָכֶ֑ם בּ֧וֹשׁוּ וְהִכָּלְמ֛וּ מִדַּרְכֵיכֶ֖ם בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Not for your sake [am] I acting, declares [the] Lord Yahweh; let it be known to you. Be ashamed and humiliated for your ways, house of Israel.

en.L: It is not for your sake that I am about to act, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}; let that be known to you! Be ashamed and humiliated because of your ways, house of Israel.
en.B: I am not about to act for your sake, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}. Be sure of that! Be ashamed and humiliated because of your conduct, house of Israel.
en.R: I want you to know that I am not doing this because of you, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}. People of Israel, you should be ashamed and embarrassed by the way you have lived.

decisions.choice: not for your sake: verse 22 again
decisions.reason: The section ends as it began (verse 22). The restoration gives Israel no ground for pride (Deuteronomy 9:4-6).

decisions.choice: the wording of verse 22 (L, B)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced repeat the wording of verse 22.

source.text: כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה בְּיוֹם֙ טַהֲרִ֣י אֶתְכֶ֔ם מִכֹּ֖ל עֲוֺנֽוֹתֵיכֶ֑ם וְהֽוֹשַׁבְתִּי֙ אֶת־הֶ֣עָרִ֔ים וְנִבְנ֖וּ הֶחֳרָבֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: On the day I cleanse you from all your iniquities, I will make the cities inhabited, and the ruins will be rebuilt.

en.L: Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: In the day of my cleansing you from all your iniquities, I will settle [people in] the cities, and the ruins will be rebuilt.
en.B: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: On the day I cleanse you from all your sins, I will cause the towns to be lived in, and the ruins will be rebuilt.
en.R: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: When I make you clean from all your sins, I will let people live in the towns again, and the ruins will be built again.

decisions.choice: on the day I cleanse you: renewal of people and land go together
decisions.reason: The inner cleansing and the rebuilding of the cities happen together. The land is restored because the people are.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD (L); The Lord GOD says this (B); This is what the Lord GOD says (R)
decisions.reason: The formula as set at 2:4. *'Awon* is "iniquity" at Literal and "guilt" or "sin" at Balanced and Readable; Balanced says "sins" here for the plural.

source.text: וְהָאָ֥רֶץ הַנְּשַׁמָּ֖ה תֵּֽעָבֵ֑ד תַּ֚חַת אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיְתָ֣ה שְׁמָמָ֔ה לְעֵינֵ֖י כָּל־עוֹבֵֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And the desolate land will be tilled, instead of being a desolation before the eyes of all who pass by.

en.L: And the desolate land will be cultivated, in place of its being a desolation before the eyes of everyone who passes by.
en.B: The land that lay desolate will be farmed again, instead of lying waste for every passerby to see.
en.R: The empty land will be farmed again. People passing by will no longer see a ruined land.

decisions.choice: in the sight of all who pass by: the reverse of the curse
decisions.reason: Passersby once looked at the ruined land in horror (5:14; Deuteronomy 29:21-23). Now they will see it farmed.

source.text: וְאָמְר֗וּ הָאָ֤רֶץ הַלֵּ֨זוּ֙ הַנְּשַׁמָּ֔ה הָיְתָ֖ה כְּגַן־עֵ֑דֶן וְהֶעָרִ֧ים הֶחֳרֵב֛וֹת וְהַֽנְשַׁמּ֥וֹת וְהַנֶּהֱרָס֖וֹת בְּצוּר֥וֹת יָשָֽׁבוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they will say, This land that was desolate has become like the garden of Eden; and the cities that were ruined and desolate and torn down are fortified [and] inhabited.

en.L: And people will say, "This land, the desolate [one], has become like the garden of Eden, and the cities that were ruined and desolate and torn down are fortified [and] inhabited."
en.B: People will say, "This land that was laid waste has become like the garden of Eden. The towns that lay ruined, desolate and torn down are now walled and lived in."
en.R: People will say, "This land was empty and ruined, but now it is like the garden of Eden. The towns were torn down and left empty, but now people live in them, and they have strong walls."

decisions.choice: like the garden of Eden: the land made new
decisions.reason: Eden is the picture of a land watered and fruitful (Genesis 2:8-10; 13:10; Isaiah 51:3). The restored land will be like the garden at the beginning. In Ezekiel, Eden also stands for the glory of the trees of 31:8-9.

decisions.choice: fortified, inhabited: the Hebrew says "fortified, they remain"
decisions.reason: The last word means "they sit" or "they are inhabited". The cities stand secure and full of people again.

decisions.choice: [and] (L)
decisions.reason: Literal brackets "and". The people's words take double quotation marks, as speech quoted inside the LORD's message.

source.text: וְיָדְע֣וּ הַגּוֹיִ֗ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִֽשָּׁאֲרוּ֮ סְבִיבוֹתֵיכֶם֒ כִּ֣י׀אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֗ה בָּנִ֨יתִי֙ הַנֶּ֣הֱרָס֔וֹת נָטַ֖עְתִּי הַנְּשַׁמָּ֑ה אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבַּ֥רְתִּי וְעָשִֽׂיתִי׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And the nations that are left around you will know that I, Yahweh, have rebuilt what was torn down, planted what was desolate. I, Yahweh, have spoken, and I will do [it].

en.L: And the nations that are left around you will know that I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have rebuilt what was torn down [and] planted the desolate [place]. I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have spoken, and I will do [it].
en.B: Then the nations still left around you will know that I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have rebuilt the ruins and replanted the wasteland. I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have spoken, and I will do it.
en.R: Then the nations around you that are still there will know that I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have rebuilt what was torn down and planted crops where the land was empty. I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have spoken, and I will do it.

decisions.choice: rebuilt and planted: the words of Jeremiah's call
decisions.reason: Building and planting are the words of hope in Jeremiah's call (Jeremiah 1:10; 31:28). The LORD will do in the land what he promised.

decisions.choice: I, the LORD, have spoken (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for this formula in Ezekiel, here with "and I will do it", as in 17:24.

source.text: כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה ע֗וֹד זֹ֛את אִדָּרֵ֥שׁ לְבֵֽית־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת לָהֶ֑ם אַרְבֶּ֥ה אֹתָ֛ם כַּצֹּ֖אן אָדָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Yet this I will let myself be sought by [the] house of Israel, to do for them: I will multiply them like a flock [of] people.

en.L: Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: This also I will let the house of Israel ask of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, to do for them: I will multiply them like a flock, [with] people.
en.B: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: This too I will let the house of Israel ask of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and I will do it for them: I will make their people as many as a flock of sheep.
en.R: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: I will let the people of Israel ask {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} for this too, and I will do it for them. I will make them grow in number, like a flock of sheep.

decisions.choice: I will let myself be sought: the LORD will answer them again
decisions.reason: In 14:3 and 20:3, 31 the LORD refused to be consulted by the elders of Israel. Now he will let them ask and will answer.

decisions.choice: like a flock: the picture of chapter 34
decisions.reason: The people are again the LORD's flock (34:31), and they will be many (36:10-11).

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD (L); The Lord GOD says this (B); This is what the Lord GOD says (R)
decisions.reason: The formula as set at 2:4. Literal brackets "with" for the Hebrew's bare "a flock, people".

source.text: כְּצֹ֣אן קָֽדָשִׁ֗ים כְּצֹ֤אן יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ בְּמ֣וֹעֲדֶ֔יהָ כֵּ֤ן תִּהְיֶ֨ינָה֙ הֶעָרִ֣ים הֶחֳרֵב֔וֹת מְלֵא֖וֹת צֹ֣אן אָדָ֑ם וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי־אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Like a flock of holy things, like the flock of Jerusalem at her appointed feasts, so will the ruined cities be full of flocks of people; and they will know that I [am] Yahweh.

en.L: Like the flock for holy offerings, like the flock of Jerusalem at her appointed feasts, so will the ruined cities be full of flocks of people; and they will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Like the flocks brought as holy offerings, like the flocks in Jerusalem at her appointed festivals, so the ruined towns will be crowded with flocks of people. Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Jerusalem used to be full of sheep at the festivals, when people brought them to offer as sacrifices. In the same way the ruined towns will be full of people. Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the flock of holy things at the appointed feasts: the sacrificial animals at the festivals
decisions.reason: At the great festivals, such as Passover, huge flocks were brought into Jerusalem to be offered (2 Chronicles 35:7-9). The ruined cities will be as crowded with people as Jerusalem was with sheep at festival time.

decisions.choice: the refrain as settled
decisions.reason: The settled wording of the refrain ("and you will know that I [am] the LORD" / "Then you will know that I am the LORD"; see 6:7).
